profile.reading:
This is a Digital Realty facility at 60 Hudson Street, New York, NY 10013, per mapping data, a landmark Manhattan telecom building long known as one of the most interconnection-dense carrier hotels in the world. This session's fetch of Digital Realty's New York metro property list did not conclusively confirm current Digital Realty ownership or a coded designation for this specific building, so no operator-confirmed square footage is reported here rather than assuming based on the building's general industry reputation.

Digital Realty Trust (NYSE: DLR, SEC CIK 1297996), headquartered at 2323 Bryan Street, Dallas, Texas, reported 310 data centers worldwide as of December 31, 2025, 221 wholly owned or consolidated and 89 in unconsolidated joint ventures, about 57.6 million rentable square feet across more than 55 metro markets including 118 US facilities, per its FY2025 Form 10-K filed with the SEC. The company operates as a colocation and wholesale landlord rather than running its own compute, distinguishing it from hyperscaler tenants such as AWS, Google, or Meta, also tracked in this registry.

This building is mapped within Digital Realty's New York/New Jersey metro footprint, which spans historic Manhattan carrier hotels and a cluster of suburban New Jersey buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township. Digital Realty markets these properties under its PlatformDIGITAL brand, positioning the metro alongside Northern Virginia, Chicago, Dallas, and Silicon Valley, all tracked elsewhere in this registry, as core hubs in its global interconnection and colocation platform.

Digital Realty's FY2025 Form 10-K identifies the United States as its largest single national market by both facility count and rentable square footage, discloses portfolio metrics by region and metro rather than by individual building, and this pattern is consistent across every Digital Realty property researched by this registry this session, not specific to this entry.

profile.regional_context: The New York/New Jersey metro is one of Digital Realty's core hub markets in its PlatformDIGITAL platform, spanning historic Manhattan carrier hotels and a cluster of suburban New Jersey buildings in Clifton and Piscataway Township. reading.body:
JFK12 is a carrier hotel at 60 Hudson Street in Manhattan, built in 1930 as the Western Union Building and now operated by Digital Realty as a major internet peering and interconnection point on the US East Coast. The operator does not publish a critical IT power capacity figure for this building, valuing it primarily for interconnection density rather than raw megawattage. No tier-1 source has confirmed individual critical IT megawatts for this facility in this research pass.

This campus does not drive AI scaling through power supply. Carrier hotels are transit and peering infrastructure, not compute platforms. The absence of published power specifications reflects the building's function: it hosts the network equipment and cross-connects that route traffic between providers and cloud platforms, not the accelerator racks and GPUs that run AI workloads.

Among 31 mapped data center facilities in New York State, only one publishes megawatt capacity, totaling 3 MW. JFK12 ranks second by published megawatts in the state, a reflection of how little critical IT power capacity is disclosed anywhere in New York. The state's data center footprint is opaque.
